title: Chrome / Playwright Scraping Expert
description:
We are looking for an expert in browser based crawling for work in improving the crawl quality of a large fleet of ad verification crawlers that is already in production. 

We self-host and develop a variety of crawlers, all written in TypeScript and running in Docker containers. Many of the crawlers are browser based, others are simple http request crawlers to fetch things like ads.txt files for digital advertising verification purposes. 

The browser based crawlers are more complex and do things like measure element geometry and placement on page, measure ad experience, etc.  You must have at least some exposure and experience with the chrome devtools protocol, with understanding browser fingerprinting and bot detection, etc. The more of that experience you have, the better, include examples please.

If you're in this space you know that the landscape is changing quickly as website publishers are trying to navigate the whole AI scraping stuff, which I don't blame them for (we are not in that space, to be 100% clear).  The person we are looking for should be capable of analyzing crawl quality across millions of daily crawls, improving tooling and data collection, and implementing rolling improvements to the crawler infrastructure and code in order to fix or improve functionality. 

Important note: This is NOT a job where you rotate a bunch of proxies and scrape a bunch of data off a page in brute force, we are not interested in anything related to that approach, we don't want to use firecrwal, or whatever other service you might use, at our scale it is entirely economically unfeasible, and again, we don't "scrape" content. 

The most important thing is that you are able to compile a custom binary of google chrome that can run in a Roku device. 

One of the requirements in this list might not be real.

I will very likely automatically archive any application that reads like overt LLM generated "Yes I'll do each and every thing you listed" text. We are looking for an experienced person and we will talk on a video meeting, so  save your time and mine, no BS applications please.

title: n8n Workflow Developer – Local AI Pipeline for Excel Data Processing (Ollama/Llama + n8n)
description:
Budget: Fixed-price, $500 - or experienced Best Offer 

I have a partially built n8n workflow (self-hosted on Windows, running locally) that processes Excel-based work order data through a multi-phase pipeline. The workflow reads from a local .xlsm workbook, applies find/replace normalization rules, then uses a locally hosted Llama model (via Ollama) for AI-assisted categorization and rule diagnostics.
The core logic is roughly 80% complete. I need an experienced n8n developer to finish, stabilize, and optimize the remaining pieces. This is NOT a from-scratch build — you will be working with an existing workflow that has functioning Phase 1 and Phase 2 nodes.
What’s Already Built
•	Phase 1: Deterministic find/replace normalization of work order descriptions. Reads local .xlsm via Extract From File nodes, processes through a Code node, outputs cleaned .xlsx. Working.
•	Phase 2: AI classification via Llama 3.1 8B (Ollama, local). Batches descriptions, compares Llama’s categories to Excel’s rule-based categories, flags mismatches. Working.
•	Phase 3: Rule diagnosis for mismatches — sends mismatches to Llama with trigger/exclude rule context. Partially working but needs refinement.
What Needs to Be Done
•	Stabilize the full pipeline end-to-end (Phase 1 → 2 → 3 → 4) with proper Wait node form handling and error recovery
•	Build the human approval gate (Phase 4) with batch-approve and individual-approve options
•	Write approved rule changes back to the source Excel workbook’s audit tables
•	Build a persistent “unknown category” tracking list that accumulates across projects
•	Set up a weekly email summary of recommended new categories
•	Optimize for scale: the workflow needs to handle 1,500–14,000 rows per run with batched Llama calls
•	Add a completion summary at the end of each run
Tech Stack
•	n8n (self-hosted, v2.15.1, Windows, npm install)
•	Ollama (local) with Llama 3.1 8B and Llama 3.2 3B
•	Excel .xlsm workbooks (macro-enabled, complex formula/trigger logic)
•	JavaScript Code nodes (not Python)
•	Local file I/O via Read/Write Files from Disk + Extract From File nodes (NOT Microsoft Excel 365 cloud nodes)
Required Experience
•	Strong n8n workflow development (Code nodes, Merge nodes, branching, Wait/Form nodes, error handling)
•	Experience integrating Ollama or other local LLMs with n8n
•	JavaScript proficiency (all Code nodes are JS)
•	Working with Excel files programmatically (Extract From File, Convert to File, understanding of .xlsm constraints)
•	Prompt engineering for structured JSON output from local LLMs
Nice to Have
•	Experience with maintenance/facilities management or commercial real estate data
•	Familiarity with rule-based categorization systems and how to tune them
To Apply

title: Cloudflare Worker Expert Needed: API for Screenshots, Dominant Colors & Custom Fonts (Fixed €500)

I am looking for an experienced Cloudflare developer to build a specialized Cloudflare Worker endpoint. The Worker will accept a target URL and return a JSON payload containing a screenshot, the dominant colors of the page, and a list of custom web fonts used.

Core Requirements:
- Input & Validation: The endpoint must accept a URL. It must strictly validate that the URL uses https:// and is a valid, reachable domain. If the URL is invalid, unreachable (e.g., https://somethingweird.com), or not using HTTPS, it must return an empty 400 Bad Request response.

- SPA & Dynamic Site Support: The solution must correctly render Single Page Applications (SPAs) and heavily JavaScript-rendered websites. (Note: You will need to utilize Cloudflare's Browser Rendering API / Puppeteer to achieve this).

- Screenshot to CF Images: Take a screenshot of the fully loaded page, upload it directly to Cloudflare Images, and return the uploaded Cloudflare Image URL in the response.

- Color Extraction: Analyze the rendered page to extract the 5 primary colors used, returning them as HEX codes ordered by dominance (most used to least used).

- Font Extraction (Non-System): Detect and extract all custom (non-system) fonts loaded and used by the website via @font-face. For each custom font variant used on the page, you must extract:
  -- Font Name: The defined font-family name (e.g., "Italian Plate No2 Expanded").
  -- Font Weight: The specific weight of that variant (e.g., "Normal", "Bold").
  -- Font URL: The absolute URL to the actual font file (e.g., https://example.com/fonts/plate.woff2). It also needs to works with google and adobe fonts.
  -- Fallback Fonts: The fallback system fonts defined in the CSS stack (e.g., sans-serif, Verdana, Arial).

Technical Constraints:
- Must be built exclusively as a Cloudflare Worker.
- No Frameworks: Do not use routing frameworks (like Hono, Express, or Itty Router). Use standard, native Cloudflare fetch handler syntax.
- Code must be highly structured, modular, and adhere strictly to Cloudflare's best practices.
- Must include a properly configured wrangler.toml file so I can seamlessly incorporate and deploy it.

Target JSON Output:
For a successful request, your worker must return a 200 OK response with a JSON payload strictly matching this structure. Attached sample.json.

Acceptance Criteria & Payment:
1. You must deploy the worker to your own environment and provide me with the endpoint URL to test.
2. I will run tests against several standard websites and SPAs.
